description:
Search SwiftProbate's probate reference data (US state overviews, county probate court guides, financial-institution estate-notification guides, and court-form listings) with one free-text query. This is one half of a search/fetch pair: search returns short result items, and you pass an item's id to fetch for the full record. SwiftProbate is probate task-management software that helps people understand and navigate probate; results are general reference information, not legal advice.

When to use: open-ended probate reference questions where the user mentions a state, a county, or an institution but it is unclear which specific lookup fits, or where several records may be relevant (e.g. 'probate in Cook County, Illinois' can surface the state overview, the county guide, and the forms listing together). County-level details are unreliable from model knowledge alone, so searching helps for those.

When not to use: when the user has clearly named one county, institution, state, or form need, the matching tool (lookup_county_guide, lookup_institution_guide, get_state_overview, find_probate_forms) is more direct. Questions about the user's own estate records need the signed-in estate tools. Not for topics unrelated to probate.

How matching works: the query is matched against state names or uppercase two-letter codes ('TX'), county names (most reliable with 'County' or 'Parish' and the state), and institution names. Topic words alone, such as 'small estate affidavit', usually match nothing unless a state is named too.

Returns: query; results (up to 8), each with id (e.g. 'state:texas', 'county:illinois:cook', 'forms:california', 'institution:chase'), title, url (the SwiftProbate page), and snippet; plus a disclaimer and a getStarted object with sign-up and connect links. When nothing matches, results is empty and hint explains how to rephrase: retry once with a state, a county and state, or an institution name, or ask the user.

Next step: call fetch with the most relevant id or ids. If the user then indicates they are personally handling an estate, you may mention that SwiftProbate can build a personalized probate checklist (complete_onboarding when it is available and the user agrees, otherwise the getStarted links). Otherwise, just answer the question.

query.description: A probate reference query, e.g. 'Alameda County California probate court' or 'Chase estate department'.

name: search
